clue.text: What could be eaten's sliced in here?

definitions.text: What could be eaten's sliced in here?

indicators.note: says the letters that follow might become something else once rearranged

parts.note: the word eaten with its S kept as a letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A riddle asking where you might find edible things cut into slices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges EATENS plus SLICED; the whole clue is also the definition, since a deli is where cooked meats are sliced to be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a shop selling prepared foods such as cold meats, which are sliced on the premises.

clue.text: Spotty daughter repeatedly needing to eat fruit

indicators.note: the doubled letter wraps round the fruit as if eating it
the daughter letter is used twice over

parts.note: an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: A spotty girl who keeps having to eat fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles D and 'to eat' puts APPLE between the two Ds.
explanation.definitionFit: Dappled means marked with spots or patches of colour.

clue.text: Left port with cargo

parts.note: Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship departing harbour fully loaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded, as a ship carrying cargo is.

clue.text: Tower in settlement overlooking a river

indicators.note: in a down clue the settlement piece sits above the rest

parts.note: a camp is a temporary settlement
the Nile is a river in Africa

explanation.surface: A tower in a village high above a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A campanile is a bell tower, especially a free-standing one beside an Italian church.

clue.text: Old Poet Laureate, English, had written rubbish before

indicators.note: the rubbish piece comes ahead of the English piece

parts.note: tat means cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: A former laureate whose earlier writing was poor stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: TAT is British slang for tasteless junk; 'had written' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahum Tate was Poet Laureate of England from 1692 until 1715.

clue.text: Frank view about art going the wrong way

indicators.note: the view piece goes around the other piece

parts.note: a sight is a view

indicators.note: the word art runs backwards

explanation.surface: An honest opinion that modern art is heading in the wrong direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but is the definition; 'going the wrong way' turns the art piece round before 'about' wraps the view around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight means honest and direct, like frank.

clue.text: World famine mustn't be allowed to start

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a dearth is a scarcity, as in famine

explanation.surface: A plea that global famine must be prevented from beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: The earth is our world, the planet we live on.

clue.text: Bloke eating heap maybe, two rounds and a biscuit

indicators.note: the bloke piece takes the others inside

parts.note: a bloke is a man
a heap is slang for an old car, so car is an example
O is round in shape, so two rounds give two Os

explanation.surface: A man munching through a pile of food, two helpings and a biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heap' is a word for a battered old car, signalled by 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a small biscuit made with ground almonds or coconut.

clue.text: Snatched scarf hanging over top of newel

indicators.note: in a down clue the scarf piece sits above the next

parts.note: a stole is a long scarf worn over the shoulders

indicators.note: only the first letter of newel is taken

explanation.surface: A scarf draped over a banister post is taken.
explanation.walkthrough: A newel is the post at the foot of a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolen means taken unlawfully, snatched.

clue.text: It shows distance walked by man going round part of St Paul's

indicators.note: one piece circles another, so the man's name wraps around the other part

parts.note: Peter is a man's name
St Paul's Cathedral in London is famous for its great dome

explanation.surface: A gadget counting the steps of a man pacing round the cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedometer is a device that counts steps and so measures how far its wearer has walked.

clue.text: Once again make a move to provide an answer

explanation.surface: A player moving again in response to an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond, which is giving an answer to some stimulus; split as re-act it means act once more.

clue.text: Gold put at the back of country carriage

indicators.note: the gold piece is placed after the country piece

parts.note: land means a country
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Gold being loaded behind a rural carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding top.

clue.text: Drink made one euphoric before the dance

indicators.note: the euphoric piece comes ahead of the dance piece

parts.note: high means elated or euphoric
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone getting merry on a drink ahead of a formal dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A highball is a long drink of spirits mixed with soda or another mixer, served in a tall glass.

clue.text: Man's erred, on reflection

indicators.note: a mirror reflection reverses, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: sinned means did wrong, erred

explanation.surface: A man admits he has done wrong after thinking it over.
explanation.definitionFit: Dennis is a man's first name, the kind of example 'man' often stands for in crosswords.

clue.text: No Parisian will accept British male misbehaving is a peer

indicators.note: the outer word takes the others inside it

parts.note: non is French for no, as a Parisian says it

indicators.note: the letters of male act up and go out of order

explanation.surface: A Frenchman refuses to tolerate a badly behaved British lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No Parisian' means the French word for no; 'misbehaving' scrambles 'male', and 'will accept' takes that and the British letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a member of the nobility, such as a duke or earl.

clue.text: Confrontation made escort depressed

parts.note: to show someone in or out is to escort them
down means low in spirits

explanation.surface: A confrontation that left a companion feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: A showdown is a final decisive confrontation between opponents.

clue.text: An expression in legal document for edifice by river?

indicators.note: the first pieces sit inside the legal document

parts.note: a will is a legal document
a term is a word or expression

explanation.surface: A phrase in a contract describing a building beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals a definition by description: a mill driven by water stands by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A watermill is a building whose machinery is driven by a water wheel, so it stands beside a river.

clue.text: Doctor supplied drug to be swallowed by poet

indicators.note: the drug goes inside the poet's name

parts.note: A. E. Housman was the English poet of A Shropshire Lad
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A doctor gives a drug to a poet to take.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a houseman is a junior hospital doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A houseman is a junior doctor working in a hospital, so a kind of doctor.

clue.text: Work surface where medicine's put before operation

indicators.note: the medicine piece is placed ahead of the operation piece

parts.note: a tablet is a dose of medicine; the 's is the link 'is'

explanation.surface: A hospital worktop where pills are laid out ahead of surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabletop is the flat upper surface of a table, used for working on.

clue.text: Row at home after meal

parts.note: a tiff is a minor row or quarrel
in means at home

explanation.surface: A domestic quarrel breaking out after dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffin is a light lunch or snack, a word from British India.

clue.text: Immediately pay the price for catching cold

indicators.note: one piece grabs another and holds it inside

parts.note: to atone is to make amends, paying for a wrong
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Being made to suffer at once for picking up a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: At once is an idiom meaning immediately, without delay.

clue.text: Determined to make a down payment

definitions.meaning: a sum paid in advance as a pledge

explanation.surface: Someone resolved to put down a deposit.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means resolute; as a noun it is a pledge paid in advance to secure a bargain.

clue.text: One meets death being eaten by shark? That's diabolical

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the shark, as if swallowed by it

parts.note: a shark is a fish
I is the Roman numeral for one
end means death

explanation.surface: Someone meeting a grisly end inside a shark, an awful fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shark?' is a definition by example, signalled by the question mark: the shark is a type of FISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiendish means devilishly cruel or wicked, just as diabolical does.

clue.text: Gloomy sweetheart embracing lover finally

indicators.note: the sweetheart piece wraps its arms round the other

parts.note: dear is a term for a sweetheart

indicators.note: only the last letter of lover is used

explanation.surface: A sad lover held in the arms of a sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic word for dreary, bleak and gloomy.

clue.text: Hollow box rattles at first

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box

indicators.note: only the opening letter of rattles is taken

explanation.surface: An empty box that rattles when shaken.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a bowl-shaped hollow in the ground.

clue.text: Follow leader of the run

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word the is taken

parts.note: a race is a run

explanation.surface: Instructions to chase the front runner.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace someone is to track or follow them.

clue.text: Champion, male coming in highest position

indicators.note: the male letter enters the champion piece

parts.note: an ace is a champion or expert

explanation.surface: A man entering as champion takes top spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the peak or highest point of something.

clue.text: Some men, animated, about to become idiotic

indicators.note: the run of letters is turned round and read backwards
only part of the words men animated is taken

explanation.surface: A group of lively men who are turning silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks ENANI out of 'men, animated' and 'about' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or senseless, the same as idiotic.

clue.text: Plan, made by one friend involving another

indicators.note: one piece wraps around and takes in the other

parts.note: a mate is a friend
a second friend: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, from china plate

explanation.surface: A scheme hatched by one friend that drags in a second.
explanation.walkthrough: CHINA for friend comes from Cockney rhyming slang, where 'china plate' rhymes with mate.
explanation.definitionFit: To machinate is to plot or scheme, which is a sly way to plan.

clue.text: Berlin carpet put out for member of British royal family

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed and laid out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A carpet from Berlin laid out for a visiting royal.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert, the German-born consort of Queen Victoria, belonged to the British royal family.
